## Week 2

Week of Sept 14

-   By W2.C1:

    -   (skim) Selections from National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. 2016. Modernizing Crime Statistics: Report 1: Defining and Classifying Crime. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press. <https://www.nationalacademies.org/projects/DBASSE-CNSTAT-13-05> .

    -   Johnson, K. R. (2021). Two Regimes of Prison Data Collection. Harvard Data Science Review, 3(3). <https://doi.org/10.1162/99608f92.72825001>

-   Sign up for a discussion leader and tech skills slots on the [assignments](assignments.qmd#leading-class-discussion) page which has a link to the [Class Leader Schedule](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1oqzW3GjvwdGwQpR57L7JWsS9Wvx-1Sehy_xs4PBAoBo/edit?gid=0#gid=0)

-   By W2.C2:

    -   Install everything you need for the [tech stack](tech-stack.qmd). Come to office hours if you're struggling.
    -   Review the information you've received about git in previous classes and come prepared to discuss what git does and why we use it.

## Week 3

Week of Sept 21

-   By W2.C1:

    -   Read Chapters 1 and 2 of *Predict and Surveil*. Bring your book to class.

-   By W2.C2:

    -   Have a first draft of research questions ready to discuss
    -   Branch with the start of your project created
    -   Have at least one meeting with your research cluster

## Week 4

Week of Sept 28

-   By W3.C1
    -   Read Chapters 3 of *Predict and Surveil*. Bring your book to class.
-   By W2.C2
    -   Stage 1 of research project DUE. This class will be a partly open work session to troubleshoot the submission of this first part of the project.
